bib.title: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces

read.skipped: Appendix B/C proofs (HiPPO diagonalisation, NPLR representations, Cauchy kernel propositions) only skimmed; math, no experimental settings. Figures not viewed, captions only.

question: Can a state space model with HiPPO state matrices be computed efficiently enough to serve as a general long-range sequence model?
hypothesis: Reparameterising A as normal plus low-rank makes the SSM stably and near-linearly computable while keeping the long-range-dependency strengths of HiPPO.
contributions: S4 parameterization: HiPPO matrix as normal plus low-rank (NPLR), diagonalised stably, SSM kernel computed via truncated generating function, Woodbury identity and a Cauchy kernel
S4 up to 30x faster with 400x less memory than the LSSL
SoTA on all LRA tasks including Path-X; SC10 raw speech
Competitive generative modeling on CIFAR-10 and WikiText-103 with 60x faster generation
Ablations showing HiPPO initialization, not NPLR form, drives accuracy

method.summary: S4 layers (H independent SSMs with 5N trainable params each, N-state, plus position-wise linear mixing and nonlinearity) are stacked as a deep sequence model. Training uses the convolutional view computed by FFT with the S4 kernel algorithm; inference uses the discretised (bilinear) recurrence with constant per-step cost. Evaluated on LRA, raw speech, pixel-level image classification, CIFAR-10 density, WikiText-103 LM and Informer forecasting benchmarks.

training.objective: classification cross-entropy (LRA, SC, sCIFAR); 256-way softmax NLL (CIFAR-10 density); next-token LM (WikiText-103); forecasting MSE
training.optimizer: AdamW (LRA, sCIFAR, WikiText-103); LAMB lr 0.005 (CIFAR density)
training.lr: LRA/other: Table 11 per task (0.0005-0.01); WikiText-103 0.0005; SSM params max 0.001

training.dropout: Table 11 per task (0-0.25); WikiText-103 0.25; CIFAR density base 0, large 0.1

training.hardware: single GPU for LRA/SC (A100 40GB for Path-X); 8x A100 for WikiText-103

results.claim: S4 averages 80.48% on Long Range Arena (original submission), versus under 60% for every baseline; the updated figure in Table 4 is 86.09.
results.setup: LRA, 6 tasks, lengths 1K-16K, single GPU per task, S4 state size N=64, hyperparameters in Table 11
results.note: Table 4 prints the updated 86.09 (S4 updated) and Table 10 lists S4 (original) 80.48; Appendix D.5 says updated results come from Gu et al. 2022 [19,20] with minor hyperparameter changes.
results.quote: averaging 80.48% compared to less than 60% for every baseline

results.claim: S4 is the first model to solve LRA Path-X (length 16384), with 88% versus 50% chance for all prior work.
results.setup: LRA Path-X, 128x128=16384 pixels flattened; original hyperparameters (Table 11: depth 6, H=256, LR 0.0005, batch 32, 100 epochs)
results.note: Updated S4 gets 96.35 on Path-X (Table 4); original 88.10 (Table 10).

results.claim: On WikiText-103, S4 replacing attention in a Transformer backbone reaches 20.95 test perplexity versus 20.51 for the Transformer, 249M vs 247M params.
results.setup: WikiText-103, 16 blocks of two S4 layers + FF, feature dim 1024, 8xA100, batch 1/GPU, context 8192, 800000 steps, AdamW lr 5e-4, dropout 0.25
results.note: Original version: batch 8, context 1024, test ppl 21.28 (Appendix D.5). Text says 'within 0.8 ppl'.
results.table: Table 8, row S4, column Test ppl.

results.claim: Attention-free SoTA on WikiText-103, beating the next best attention-free model by over 2 perplexity.
results.metric: perplexity gap to best prior attention-free
results.setup: WikiText-103 test; next best TaLK Conv. 23.3 ppl, 240M params
results.quote:
setting SoTA for attention-free models by over

results.claim: S4 generates tokens/pixels about 60x faster than a vanilla Transformer by switching to recurrent mode (constant memory and compute per step).
results.setup: WikiText-103 (tokens/s, Table 8) and CIFAR-10 (images/s, Table 7), single A100, batch maximised to fit memory; Transformer timing excludes embedding/softmax layers so is slightly favourable to the baseline
results.quote: with S4 around 60× faster than a vanilla Transformer

results.claim: S4 reaches 91.13% on sequential CIFAR (sCIFAR) with no 2-D bias, versus 62.2 for a Transformer and 84.65 for LSSL.
results.setup: Pixel-level 1-D CIFAR-10, depth 6, H=1024, LN, dropout 0.25, LR 0.01, batch 50, 200 epochs, AdamW, no augmentation
results.note: Text prints 91%/91.12% for no augmentation (Sec 4.3), Table 6 prints 91.13; 93.16% with mild augmentation (flips, random crops).

results.claim: S4 (large) gets 2.85 bits per dim on CIFAR-10 density estimation with no 2-D inductive bias.
results.setup: 3072 RGB subpixels flattened; UNet-style S4 blocks, base B=8 H=128, large B=16 H=192, LAMB lr 0.005, 256-way softmax loss
results.quote:
competitive with the best
autoregressive models (2.85 bits per dim)

results.claim: S4 is up to 30x faster with 400x less memory than the LSSL.
results.setup: Single forward+backward pass of one layer, single A100; Table 2 gives 29.6x speed and 392x memory at H=512 (LSSL 140.7 ms / 13140 MB vs S4 4.75 ms / 33.5 MB); S4 N is N/4 of LSSL to parameter-match
results.quote:
S4 is up to 30× faster with 400× less memory
usage

results.setup: SC10 10-class subset of Speech Commands, raw 16000-sample signals; depth 6, H=128, BN, dropout 0.1, LR 0.01, batch 20, 150 epochs
results.note: Appendix D.5 says to cite Table 11 of Gu et al. 2022 [19] (full 35-class SC) instead.

results.setup: Informer benchmark (ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, Weather, ECL), univariate and multivariate; context concatenated with F mask tokens, last F outputs used

results.setup: Univariate Weather, horizon 720: S4 0.245 MSE vs Informer 0.359 (Table 9)

results.claim: Ablation: full S4 with HiPPO initialization reaches 84.27% test accuracy on sequential CIFAR-10 with 100K parameters and 0.1 dropout; random inits trail by over 15% validation accuracy.
results.setup: sequential CIFAR-10, plateau LR scheduler, dropout 0.1; random NPLR matrices still perform poorly, so gains come from HiPPO init, not the NPLR form
results.quote: achieves 84.27% test accuracy with just 100K parameters

results.claim: S4 matches a larger ResNet-18 on sequential CIFAR (7.9M vs 11.0M params): 91.12% vs 89.46% without augmentation, 93.16% vs 95.62% with it; swapping BatchNorm for LayerNorm gives 90.46% vs 79.52%.
S4 has O~(N+L) computation and O(N+L) memory for the convolution kernel, and O(N) per recurrence step.
results.setup: Theorems 2 and 3; Normal Plus Low-Rank A reduced to Cauchy kernel via Woodbury and FFT; current implementation uses naive O(NL) Cauchy via pykeops, not the fast algorithm
results.quote: This results in ˜O(N + L) computation and O(N + L) memory usage

results.claim: HiPPO matrix change alone lifts a plain SSM from 60% to 98% on sequential MNIST (reported from the LSSL work).
results.setup: LSSL, A random vs HiPPO matrix
results.quote: improved its performance on the sequential MNIST benchmark from 60% to 98%

limits: Authors concede a perplexity gap to Transformers on WikiText-103 (20.95 vs 20.51) and say S4 may not suit all data types.
Implementation uses the naive O(NL) Cauchy kernel via pykeops; the asymptotically fast stable algorithms are not implemented on GPU, so near-linear complexity is theoretical.
The original S4 NPLR parameterization can be numerically unstable with eigenvalues in the right half-plane; follow-up changes Lambda-PQ* to Lambda-PP*.
No seeds, variance or significance reported; baselines for speech were swept by the authors with limited grids and several baselines could not train on one GPU.
LRA and SC results have since been updated; the paper says to cite Gu et al. 2022 for SC (full 35-class) and the updated LRA numbers.
WikiText-103 scale is 250M params; no large-scale pretraining or in-context behaviour tested.
Transformer generation baseline timing excludes embedding and softmax layers.
